source.publication: 2025 Expanded Instructions (IA 1040) and the 2025 IA 1040 Iowa Individual Income Tax Return
source.section: IA 1040 form PDF p.1 Step 3 lines a, b, d; form PDF p.2 lines 1c, 2-5, 7, 8, 11, 12; Instructions PDF p.8 Step 3; PDF p.9-10 lines 2-4; PDF p.12 line 5 ('Iowa now has a flat tax rate of 3.8%'); PDF p.18 line 12; PDF p.8 Step 3 a: status 4 'should enter 2'

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (you) 60,000.00 = 60,000.00. Federal taxable income = 60,000.00 - standard deduction 23,625.00 = 36,375.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). IA 1040 filing status 4 (head of household). Step 3 line a personal credits 1 x 40.00 = 40.00; line b 0 x 20.00 = 0.00 (65 or older on or before January 1, 2026; nobody blind); line c no dependents; line d and line 8 = 40.00. Line 1c federal AGI 60,000.00; line 2 federal taxable income 36,375.00. Schedule 1: no additions or subtractions. Schedule 1 line 21 net modifications = 0.00; line 3 = 0.00. Line 4 Iowa taxable income = 36,375.00 + (0.00) = 36,375.00. Line 5 tax = 3.8% x 36,375.00 = 1,382.25; line 7 = 1,382.25. Line 11 total credits 40.00; line 12 balance = 1,382.25 - 40.00 = 1,342.25. State income tax 1,342.25 (no line 13-17 credits; line 19 school district or EMS surtax is local, not computed). The form allows whole-dollar rounding; expected keeps the cents. Low-income exemption and alternate tax (PDF p.10-13): line 4 36,375.00 + federal deduction 23,625.00 = 60,000.00, against 13,500.00: not exempt; alternate tax 4.3% x (60,000.00 - 13,500.00) = 1,999.50, not smaller than the 3.8% tax. The form's figure is 1,302.25: status 4 enters 2 personal credits (80.00). The projection's relief is one credit per person, so it gives 40.00 and is 40.00 too high.
accepted_approximations: The extra 40 personal credit for head of household; a relief here cannot test filing status. Leaves the tax 40 too high for those filers.
School district and county EMS surtaxes (a percentage of the tax, form line 19) are local and out of scope (issue #1).
